size_rationale: Medium because the config is read in one place (config.js) and used in another (token generation), so the cause sits one step away from the 401s the prompt describes.
prompt: Users are logged out straight away: the access token returned by login or register is rejected with 401 'Please authenticate' on the very next request, and `tokens.access.expires` in the login response equals the time of the request. Refresh tokens are unaffected.

root_cause.detail: config.jwt.accessExpirationMinutes reads envVars.JWT_ACCESS_EXPIRATION, a key that is never set (the validated key is JWT_ACCESS_EXPIRATION_MINUTES); the value is undefined, moment().add(undefined, 'minutes') adds nothing, and access tokens expire at issue time.

fail_to_pass: tests/integration/auth.test.js > Auth middleware > should call next with no errors if access token is valid
tests/integration/user.test.js > User routes > POST /v1/users > should return 201 and successfully create new user if data is ok
oracle.cmd: npx jest tests/integration/auth.test.js tests/integration/user.test.js -t 'should call next with no errors if access token is valid|should return 201 and successfully create new user if data is ok'
